prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core message: Westminster is “broken” by Brexit; Scotland should decide its own future. The SNP seeks a 2020 independence referendum via a lawful transfer of powers (Section 30), is open to a progressive alliance to keep the Tories out, and will push to keep Scotland in or close to the EU.

Brexit and Europe
- Support a UK-wide second EU referendum with Remain on the ballot; revoke Article 50 if the alternative is no-deal.
- Protect Single Market/Customs Union ties and align with EU standards.
- Argue Brexit harms jobs, living standards, rights and the NHS; oppose US trade deals that threaten standards.

Democracy and constitutional change
- Independence to secure governments Scotland votes for, full control over tax/social security, EU membership, and no Trident.
- Reform UK democracy: replace First Past the Post with STV, abolish the House of Lords, votes at 16, extend Westminster voting rights to EU citizens/settled residents, establish an independent debates commission.
- Defend human rights: keep the Human Rights Act/ECHR; incorporate UNCRC; tackle racism and bigotry.

Economy, tax and public investment
- End austerity; reverse real-terms cuts to Scotland’s budget; invest in services and wellbeing.
- Fair taxation: reject unfunded tax cuts for the wealthy, crack down on avoidance/evasion, review HMRC closures, reform Companies House, modernise digital tax.
- Support SMEs: increase Employment Allowance; provide Brexit advisory support; sector deals; fairer city/region deal funding.
- Infrastructure and digital: increase capital borrowing; back the Scottish National Investment Bank; expand gigabit broadband/4G/5G and affordable tariffs; reclassify internet as an essential service.

Work, wages and corporate reform
- Devolve employment law; raise the statutory living wage to at least the real Living Wage; end zero-hours exploitation; strengthen gig-economy rights; enforce equal pay with fines.
- Improve corporate culture: worker representation on boards, fair executive pensions, climate-risk disclosures, stronger late-payment protections.

NHS and social security
- Match Scottish per-capita NHS spending UK-wide; legislate an NHS Protection Act to exclude health from trade deals; compensate contaminated blood victims.
- Reform welfare: scrap the two-child cap/rape clause; halt/fix Universal Credit; end sanctions and the benefit freeze; inflation-uplift benefits; humane terminal illness rules.

Pensions
- Protect the Triple Lock; oppose state pension age rises; back WASPI justice; restore Pension Credit changes; fund free TV licences for over-75s; expand auto-enrolment.

Families, education and children
- Expand early learning and childcare to 1,140 hours; close the attainment gap; keep free higher education.
- Tackle child poverty (Scottish Child Payment) and reintroduce UK child poverty targets.
- Strengthen parental rights: longer, better-paid maternity/paternity/shared leave, neonatal leave, stronger redundancy protections.

Health, addiction and justice
- Devolve drug policy; pilot supervised drug consumption facilities; treat drug deaths as a public health emergency.
- Maintain law and order; protect cross-border security tools post-Brexit.

Climate and energy
- Meet Scotland’s world-leading targets (75% emissions cut by 2030; net zero by 2045); align UK policy; Green Energy Deal; accelerate CCS; earlier EV transition; greener tax incentives; mass tree planting; oppose fracking.
- Boost renewables (onshore wind/solar access to CfD; wave/tidal support); reform transmission charging; deliver island interconnectors.

Rural, food, fisheries and tourism
- Protect agricultural funding (including convergence uplift); uphold PGIs; maintain high standards; compensate sectors hit by tariffs; ban trophy imports.
- Fisheries: Scottish control in negotiations; fair access and compliance; protect seafood exports and workforce.
- Tourism: defend freedom of movement; consider VAT cut for hospitality.

Migration, asylum and refugees
- Devolve migration; oppose the hostile environment/minimum salary thresholds; end indefinite detention; expand family reunion/Dubs; right to work for asylum seekers; pilot Scottish Visa.

Defence, foreign policy and veterans
- Scrap Trident; invest in conventional defence and Scottish shipyards; uphold 0.7% aid, add a Climate Justice Fund.
- Support veterans: use vacant MoD homes for homeless ex-service personnel; secure immigration rights for Commonwealth personnel.

Record
- SNP MPs led on blocking no-deal, overturning unlawful prorogation, protecting EU citizens’ fees, securing farm funding, VAT relief for Police/Fire, and resisting welfare cuts.
